weeks.title: Week 1: Core Concepts
weeks.html:
Executive Summary

Summit Development Group faces sophisticated financing for their largest project: a $75M mixed-use development requiring multiple sources, complex guarantees, and careful covenant management across their portfolio.

Project Overview

Summit Gateway: 200-unit luxury apartments + 50,000 sq ft retail

Location: Prime downtown with transit access

Total Cost: $75,000,000

Timeline: 30-month development and construction

Exit Strategy: Hold for cash flow or sell at stabilization

Company Financial Position

Summit Development Group - Consolidated:

Total Assets: $125,000,000

Total Debt: $78,000,000

Equity: $47,000,000

Annual Revenue: $95,000,000

EBITDA: $18,500,000

Debt Service: $8,200,000

Current DSCR: 2.26x

Financing Challenge

Proposed Structure:

Senior Construction: $45,000,000 (60% LTC)

- Rate: Prime + 1.75% (currently 7.0%)

- Term: 30 months interest-only

- Covenants: DSCR >1.5x, Working Capital >$8M

Mezzanine: $15,000,000 (20% LTC)

- Rate: 12% current + 3% PIK

- Term: 36 months

- Equity Kicker: 10% profits after 12% IRR

Developer Equity: $15,000,000 (20% LTC)

- Cash: $10,000,000

- Deferred Fees: $5,000,000

Required Analysis

Task 1: Structure Optimization Evaluate proposed structure considering:

Cost of capital optimization

Risk allocation among sources

Covenant compliance across portfolio

Exit strategy alignment

Task 2: Cash Flow Modeling Develop 36-month projections including:

Construction draws and interest payments

Existing portfolio cash flows

Covenant compliance testing

Sensitivity analysis for variables

Task 3: Credit Enhancement Strategy Design package including:

Performance guarantees required

Letter of credit requirements

Personal/corporate guarantee optimization

Alternative credit support options

Task 4: Risk Management Identify and mitigate:

Interest rate exposure

Construction cost overruns

Market/leasing risks

Refinancing risk planning

Expected Results

Base Case Projections:

Year 1: $(8,500,000) net cash flow

Year 2: $(12,200,000) peak construction

Year 3: $15,800,000 lease-up/stabilization

Covenant Analysis:

Minimum DSCR: 1.47x (Month 18)

Working Capital Low: $7.2M (Month 24)

Maximum Leverage: 1.85x (Month 20)

Recommended Optimization:

Modified Structure:

Senior: $42M (improved covenant to 1.35x DSCR)

Mezzanine: $18M (with deferred interest option)

Equity: $15M (accelerated timing)

Reserve: $2M (covenant cushion)

Benefits:

- Maintained compliance throughout

- Lower blended cost: 8.9% vs 9.4%

- Enhanced refinancing flexibility

- Improved risk-adjusted returns

Implementation Success Metrics

Maintain covenant compliance throughout construction

Achieve 80%+ occupancy by Month 30

Complete within 5% of budget

Generate 18%+ IRR for developer equity

This comprehensive case demonstrates the complexity of large-scale construction financing and the CFO's critical role in structuring, managing, and optimizing capital throughout the development process.
